mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over two months indicates a restrictive monetary policy with falling inflation, which may signal recession risk and result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals robust demand growth, which boosts earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days under a moderate inflation regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above 12-month MA for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months in a moderate inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals an expansion in economic output and corporate capacity, which supports higher earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months of INDPRO increases.
